common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Corneal abrasion.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Corneal foreign body without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any whitish infiltrate under the defect would suggest infection rather than simple abrasion.
management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Corneal Abrasion of the right eye, superficial epithelial defect
Perform fluorescein staining under cobalt blue light (visualize green epithelial scratch, confirm no infiltrate)
Provide topical erythromycin ointment and oral analgesia; consider a short-course cycloplegic only for clinically significant traumatic iritis or photophobia
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Corneal Abrasion of the right eye, superficial epithelial defect. severe eye pain, watering, and light sensitivity after being poked in the eye. 32M presents with severe right eye pain, constant tearing, and photophobia that started immediately after his 2-year-old toddler accidentally poked him in the right eye with a finger.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Corneal Abrasion of the right eye, superficial epithelial defect.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Corneal Abrasion of the right eye, superficial epithelial defect.
reference_soap.plan: Check visual acuity, pupil shape/reactivity, and fluorescein staining under cobalt-blue light to identify an epithelial defect and exclude an infiltrate. Provide topical erythromycin ointment and oral analgesia; consider a short-course cycloplegic only for clinically significant traumatic iritis or photophobia. Do not patch. Urgently refer for reduced vision, an irregular pupil, hyphema, suspected penetrating injury, or an infiltrate.
